prompt: In three sentences, explain why the sky is blue.
content: The sky is blue because molecules in Earth's atmosphere scatter sunlight in all directions, and shorter wavelengths of light (blue and violet) scatter more strongly than longer wavelengths. This effect, called Rayleigh scattering, occurs because scattering intensity is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength. Although violet light scatters even more than blue, the sky appears blue because the sun emits less violet light, our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some violet is absorbed in the upper atmosphere.
